prompt.es: Redacta los hallazgos y límites de la encuesta sobre el sueño.

answer.text: Our survey of two hundred pupils produced two main findings. First, sixty per cent of the pupils sleep less than eight hours a night. Second, among the pupils who sleep little, twice as many girls as boys say that they feel tired in class. These figures suggest that a lack of sleep may affect how pupils feel at school, and they appear to show that girls are more affected than boys. However, the results have an important limitation. All the pupils came from one school, and they described their own sleep, so the data may be biased. For this reason, we cannot say that sleep causes tiredness; we can only say that the two seem to be linked. Further research with a larger sample from several schools would be needed before we can speak for all teenagers. In short, the findings are interesting, but they should be read with care.
accepted: Our survey of two hundred pupils produced two main findings. First, sixty per cent of the pupils sleep less than eight hours a night. Second, among the pupils who sleep little, twice as many girls as boys say that they feel tired in class. These figures suggest that a lack of sleep may affect how pupils feel at school, and they appear to show that girls are more affected than boys. However, the results have an important limitation. All the pupils came from one school, and they described their own sleep, so the data may be biased. For this reason, we cannot say that sleep causes tiredness; we can only say that the two seem to be linked. Further research with a larger sample from several schools would be needed before we can speak for all teenagers. In short, the findings are interesting, but they should be read with care.

We asked two hundred pupils about their sleep and found two things. To begin with, 60 per cent of them sleep for less than eight hours. In addition, among those pupils, double the number of girls compared with boys reported feeling tired during lessons. The data indicate that short sleep could be connected with tiredness in class, and girls seem to be more affected than boys. Nevertheless, there is a limitation: only one school took part, and the pupils described their own hours, so the answers may not be accurate. Because of this, the results do not prove a cause. More research with a larger sample from different schools would help to show whether the same pattern appears elsewhere. To sum up, the findings are useful, but they must be treated with care.
